reason: At base the bug exists: REGEX_FORMAT matched Y{1,4} but format() only handled YY/YYYY, so Y/YYY fell through to the timezone-offset fallback and returned a UTC offset instead of literal 'Y' / 'YY'+'Y'.
After the fix REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' is left literal and 'YYY' becomes YY(year)+'Y', matching the expected output.
The PR only refactors percent-decoding into a shared tryDecodeURIComponent utility; behavior (decoding %20 to a space) is unchanged, so the route param is still decoded.
The refactor is behavior-preserving; %20 is still decoded to a space after the change, so the decoded param contains the literal space.
At base reschedule() writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so the in-memory entry's #score/#at return the stale pre-reschedule value.
The fix sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby, so the in-memory entry reflects the newly requested reschedule time immediately.
The PR only changes Range-header whitespace parsing; Content-Type charset parsing is unrelated and an established feature, so the test passes independently of this revision.
Same as base: the PR touches only Range parsing, not Content-Type charset parsing, which is an unrelated established feature.
PR only changes download-failure logging messages; zip mtime preservation is unrelated. Assuming the archiver preserves mtimes, the test passes at both revisions.
Identical to base reasoning: the logging-only PR does not affect archive mtime behavior, so the test outcome is unchanged at head.
PR changes CredentialCache path comparison; async JSON deserialization with a nullable parent property is an unrelated core feature that should succeed.
Same as base: the CredentialCache PR is unrelated to System.Text.Json deserialization, which should succeed regardless of revision.
PR fixes FETCH FIRST on an empty WITH HOLD cursor; INET <<= ANY is an unrelated core SQL operator that should parse, execute, and return true.
Same as base: the cursor fix does not affect INET containment with ANY, which should succeed at head too.
At base NO_PROXY='::1' was wrapped as 'all://*::1', which a later URL-parse step could not interpret, raising an error; the test expects successful client construction.
After the fix '::1' is recognized as IPv6 and mounted as 'all://[::1]', so the client constructs without error and bypasses proxy for the loopback correctly.
At base, passing flags=re.DOTALL to Series.str.match raised due to a strict flag-equality check; the test expects DOTALL to be honored, not rejected.
After the fix, regex flags other than IGNORECASE (e.g. DOTALL) are honored, so 'a.c' with DOTALL matches 'a\nc' but not 'ac'.
At base the recursive result-parent bug for a group in the middle of a chain malforms the result tree, so serialize/reconstruct would not preserve all four child results.
The fix corrects result parents for a group in the middle of a chain, so the reconstructed result tree preserves every child result.
The '--' appears mid-arguments, not as the first argument; that normal case already works via trailing-values handling, so both positionals capture correctly at base.
Same as base: the PR only fixes the first-argument '--' case, leaving this mid-stream '--' scenario passing at head too.
At base a late OSC11 response calls nvim_set_option_value('background',...) directly, which triggers OptionSet, matching the test's expectation that OptionSet fires.
The fix wraps the background assignment in :noautocmd, suppressing the OptionSet event; the test expects OptionSet to fire, so it fails after the change.
PR only reorders compile-time @derive dependency checks; required-field validation behavior is unchanged, so the changeset is still flagged invalid with a blank error.
Same as base: the compile-time dependency reordering does not affect runtime required-field validation, which still marks the changeset invalid.
